question.problem: Use Green's theorem to evaluate ${∮}_{C}(2x+{e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡y)\,dx+(x+{e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡y)\,dy,$ where $C$ is the boundary of the trapezoid with vertices at $(0,1),$ $(0,-5),$ $(4,-1)$ and $(4,1).$
question.worked_solution:
Let $C$ be a positively oriented, piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in the plane, and let $D$ be the region bounded by $C.$ If $P$ and $Q$ have continuous first partial derivatives on an open region containing $D$, then Green's theorem states that

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,dx+Q\,dy={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\text{d}A.
$$

The region $D$ and the curve $C$ for this case are shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14120089/assets/acd7ae0cc90007b9f710f242ab1f0498b2439cdbb8951df388b9d8d0588d553f.png)

First, notice that we can rewrite our integral as follows:

$$
{∮}_{C}F\cdot dr={∮}_{C}(2x+{e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡y)\,dx+(x+{e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡y)\,dy
$$

We have that $P(x,y)=2x+{e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡y$ and $Q(x,y)=x+{e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡y.$ Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂P}{∂y}={e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡y,\,\frac{∂Q}{∂x} & =1+{e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡y.\end{aligned}
$$

We can express the region $D$ as a type I region as follows:

$$
D=\{(x,y):0\le x\le 4,\,x-5\le y\le 1\}
$$

Therefore, applying Green's Theorem, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{∮}_{C}(2x+{e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡y)\,dx+(x+{e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡y)\,dy & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(1+{e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡y-{e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}1\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}{\int }_{x-5}^{1}\text{d}y\,\text{d}x \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}[y]_{x-5}^{1}\,dx \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{4}(6-x)\,dx \\  & ={[6x-\frac{{x}^{2}}{2}]}_{0}^{4} \\  & =24-\frac{16}{2} \\  & =16.\end{aligned}
$$
